title: Mechanistic Interpretability Needs Philosophy
abstract: arXiv:2506.18852v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Mechanistic interpretability (MI) aims to explain how trained neural networks work by uncovering their underlying mechanisms. As the field grows in influence, it is increasingly important to examine not just models themselves, but the assumptions, concepts and explanatory strategies implicit in MI research. We argue that mechanistic interpretability needs philosophy as an ongoing partner in clarifying its concepts, refining its methods, and navigating the epistemic and ethical complexities of interpreting AI systems. There is significant unrealised potential for progress in MI to be gained through deeper engagement with philosophers and philosophical frameworks. Taking three open problems from the MI literature as examples, this paper illustrates the value philosophy can add to MI research, and outlines a path toward deeper interdisciplinary dialogue.

translated_title: 机制可解释性需要哲学
translated_abstract: 机制可解释性旨在通过揭示训练后的神经网络背后的底层机制来解释其工作原理。随着该领域影响力的不断增长，不仅审视模型本身，审视机制可解释性研究中隐含的假设、概念和解释策略也变得日益重要。我们认为，机制可解释性需要哲学作为持续合作的伙伴，以澄清其概念、完善其方法，并应对解释人工智能系统时涉及的认识论和伦理复杂性。通过与哲学家和哲学框架的深入接触，机制可解释性的进步仍具有巨大的未开发潜力。本文以机制可解释性文献中的三个开放性问题为例，展示了哲学能够为机制可解释性研究带来的价值，并勾勒出一条通向更深入跨学科对话的路径。
tldr: 该论文主张机制可解释性研究需要与哲学建立持续的合作关系，借助哲学澄清概念、完善方法并应对认识论与伦理层面的复杂性，从而释放该领域尚未实现的巨大发展潜力。
en_tdlr: This paper argues that mechanistic interpretability needs philosophy as an ongoing partner to clarify its concepts, refine its methods, and navigate epistemic and ethical complexities, unlocking significant unrealized potential for the field's progress.
